docs.title: Home
docs.text: Welcome to the documentation for the nf-illumina2lineage pipeline.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This repository provides a complete pipeline for assembling and analyzing the genome of SARS-CoV-2 using Illumina paired-end sequencing data. It includes steps for quality control, mapping, variant calling, primer clipping, consensus sequence generation, lineage annotation, and phylogenetic analysis.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Automated environment setup using pixi
  • Comprehensive quality control with fastqc and fastp
  • Mapping and visualization using minimap2, samtools, and IGV
  • Primer sequence clipping for clean alignments
  • Variant calling with freebayes
  • Consensus sequence generation and lineage assignment with pangolin
  • Phylogenetic analysis and multiple sequence alignment with mafft and iqtree
  • Clear documentation and modular structure

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Operating System: Linux (tested on Fedora 38)
  • Processor: Intel i5 or higher, with multithreading support
  • Memory: Minimum 8 GB

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
The pipeline requires the following tools, managed via mamba:

  • QC: fastqc, fastp, multiqc
  • Mapping: minimap2, samtools, bamclipper
  • Variant Calling: freebayes, vcftools, bcftools
  • Sequence Analysis: mafft, iqtree, pangolin
  • Visualization: IGV

docs.title: Input Data
docs.text:
• Illumina paired-end sequencing data
  • SARS-CoV-2 reference genome (NCBI accession: NC_045512.2)

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• Quality control reports (.html, .json)
  • Aligned sequences in BAM and VCF formats
  • Consensus sequences in FASTA format
  • Lineage annotations
  • Phylogenetic trees and visualizations

docs.title: About
docs.text: This pipeline was developed as part of the SARS-2 Bioinformatics & Data Science course offered jointly by Freie Universität Berlin and the Robert Koch Institute.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: The aim was to create a reproducible, modular, and fully-documented pipeline for assembling and analyzing SARS-CoV-2 genomes from Illumina paired-end sequencing data using best-practice bioinformatics tools.

docs.title: Lineage & QC
docs.text: This section explains how the pipeline handles lineage annotation and consensus sequence quality assessment.

docs.title: Lineage Annotation with Pangolin
docs.text: pangolin is used to assign SARS-CoV-2 lineages based on the consensus sequences generated by the pipeline.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: • consensus-seqs.fasta (combined consensus sequences for all samples)

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• lineage_report.csv — Pangolin lineage calls with sample metadata
  • Additional summary files: summary.csv, pangolin.json (optional)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Pangolin is executed via the following command in the pipeline:

pangolin -t 8 consensus-seqs.fasta

docs.title: Consensus QC with PRESIDENT
docs.text: PRESIDENT evaluates consensus sequences by comparing them to the reference genome.

docs.title: Checks Performed
docs.text:
• Pairwise nucleotide identity
  • Ambiguous base counts
  • Masked regions

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
• reference.fasta
  • consensus-seqs.fasta

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• Summary reports written to the output/ directory
  • .html and tabular output formats depending on PRESIDENT version

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Executed as part of the pipeline:

president -r reference.fasta -q consensus-seqs.fasta -t 8 -a -p output/ -f consensus_

📈 These results help assess sequence reliability before downstream analysis like phylogenetics.

docs.title: downloadData/Content: Raw Sequencing Reads
docs.text:
• <sample_id>_R1_001.fastq.gz / _R2_001.fastq.gz: The original, unprocessed sequencing data from the sequencer or repository (e.g., SRA/ENA).
  • Format: FASTQ (gzip compressed).
  • Use: The starting point for the entire pipeline.

docs.title: referenceGenome/Content: Viral Reference
docs.text:
• reference.fasta: The standard SARS-CoV-2 genome sequence (NC_045512.2).
  • Use: Used as the template for mapping reads and calling variants.

docs.title: 2. Pre-processing & Alignment####qc/Content: Quality Control & Trimming
docs.text:
• <sample_id>.fastp.html: An interactive HTML report visualizing read quality before and after trimming. Look here to check adapter removal and read quality scores.
  • <sample_id>.R1/R2.clean.fastq.gz: The "clean" sequencing reads. Adapters have been trimmed, and low-quality bases removed. These are used for mapping.

docs.title: mapping/Content: Genome Alignment
docs.text:
• <sample_id>.sorted.bam: The Binary Alignment Map (BAM) file. It contains the clean reads aligned to the reference genome, sorted by coordinate.
  • Use: Essential for visualization in tools like IGV (Integrative Genomics Viewer) to see coverage depth and mutations.

docs.title: primerClipping/Content: PCR Primer Removal
docs.text:
• <sample_id>.primerclipped.bam: A modified BAM file where PCR primer sequences have been "soft-clipped" (masked).
  • Why this matters: Amplicon sequencing uses synthetic primers to amplify the virus. If these synthetic sequences aren't removed, they can mask real mutations or introduce false ones.

docs.title: 3. Consensus & Analysis####consensusGeneration/Content: Individual Viral Genomes
docs.text: • <sample_id>.consensus.fasta: The reconstructed viral genome for a single specific sample. This sequence represents the specific variant of the virus found in that patient/sample.

docs.title: mergeConsensus/Content: Aggregate Genomes
docs.text:
• consensus-seqs.fasta: A Multi-FASTA file containing the consensus sequences of all processed samples combined into one file.
  • Use: This is the primary input for downstream phylogenetic analysis and lineage assignment.

docs.title: 4. Classification & Quality Assessment####pangolinLineage/Content: Variant Classification
docs.text:
• lineage_report.csv: A spreadsheet generated by the Pangolin tool.
  • Key Columns to check:
  • lineage: The assigned Pango lineage (e.g., B.1.1.7, BA.5).
  • scorpio_call: The WHO variant name (e.g., Alpha, Omicron).
  • ambiguity_score: Quality metric indicating how many "N" (unknown) bases affected the call.

docs.title: consensusQC/Content: Genome Quality Metrics (Tool: President)
docs.text:
• consensus_report.tsv: A tabular summary of genome quality. Checks for "N" content (ambiguous bases) and frameshifts.
  • consensus_valid.fasta: Genomes that PASSED quality control checks.
  • consensus_invalid.fasta: Genomes that FAILED checks (usually due to low coverage resulting in too many Ns).

docs.title: phylogeny/Content: Evolutionary Tree
docs.text:
• phylo.treefile: A phylogenetic tree file generated by IQ-TREE.
  • Use: Can be opened in tree viewers like FigTree or Dendroscope to visualize how the samples are related to each other evolutionarily.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: This section lists the configurable parameters used in the pipeline. These can be adjusted using a custom configuration file or passed directly via the command line.

docs.title: Core Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description reads *.fastq.gz Glob pattern to match input FASTQ files reference reference.fasta Reference genome in FASTA format threads 8 Number of threads to use for multithreaded tools

docs.title: Default Configuration
docs.text:
nextflow run main.nf -profile pixi

or 

pixi run run-pipeline

💡 All parameters can also be set directly via -params flag or in nextflow.config.

docs.title: Process Details
docs.text: This section describes each Nextflow process in the pipeline, including their inputs, outputs, and core functionality.

docs.title: downloadData
docs.text:
Purpose: Downloads the "illumina-amplicon-capture-wgs.tar.gz" dataset from OSF by default.

  • Input: None
  • Output: Raw .fastq.gz files

docs.title: referenceGenome
docs.text:
Purpose: Download SARS-CoV-2 reference genome (NC_045512.2) using NCBI Entrez Direct.

  • Input: None
  • Output: reference.fasta

docs.title: qc
docs.text:
Purpose: Quality control and cleaning of raw sequencing reads.

  • Input: Paired-end FASTQ files
  • Output:
    • Cleaned FASTQ files (pair*.R1/2.clean.fastq.gz)
    • FastQC reports (.html, .zip)
    • Fastp reports (.json, .html)
    • MultiQC summary

docs.title: mapping
docs.text:
Purpose: Align reads to reference genome and produce sorted, indexed BAM files.

  • Input: Cleaned FASTQ files, reference.fasta
  • Output: Sorted and indexed BAM files (.sorted.bam, .bai)

docs.title: primerClipping
docs.text:
Purpose: Clip primer sequences using a CleanPlex BEDPE file and bamclipper. Automatically downloads the cleanplex.amplicons.bedpe file and converts it to Unix format during execution

  • Input: Sorted BAM files
  • Output: Primer-clipped BAM files (.primerclipped.bam)

docs.title: variantCalling
docs.text:
Purpose: Call variants from aligned BAM files using freebayes.

  • Input: Primer-clipped BAM files, reference.fasta
  • Output: Raw VCF files (${sample_id}.vcf)

docs.title: consensusGeneration
docs.text:
Purpose: Generate consensus sequences using bcftools from VCFs.

  • Input: VCF files, reference.fasta
  • Output: FASTA files for consensus sequences (${sample_id}.consensus.fasta)

docs.title: mergeConsensus
docs.text:
Purpose: Merge consensus sequences from multiple samples into a single FASTA file.

  • Input: FASTA files for consensus sequences (${sample_id}.consensus.fasta)
  • Output: Combined consensus FASTA file (combined_consensus.fasta)

docs.title: pangolinLineage
docs.text:
Purpose: Assign SARS-CoV-2 lineages using pangolin.

  • Input: Combined consensus FASTA file
  • Output: lineage_report.csv, optional TSV and summary files

docs.title: consensusQC
docs.text:
Purpose: Assess consensus quality using president.

  • Input: Consensus FASTA, reference.fasta
  • Output: QC summary in output/ folder

docs.title: phylogeny
docs.text:
Purpose: Perform multiple sequence alignment and build phylogenetic tree.

  • Input: Consensus FASTA file
  • Output: alignment.fasta, IQ-TREE outputs (e.g., .treefile, .log)

For a visual overview, see the Workflow section.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This guide will help you get the pipeline up and running as quickly as possible. To use your own data, you must override the input parameters or modify the downloadData process, as the current script hardcodes a download from OSF.

docs.title: Step 1: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/bibymaths/nf-illumina2lineage.git
cd nf-illumina2lineage

docs.title: Step 2: Install Pixi
docs.text:
Install Pixi using the official installer:

curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | bash

Restart your shell, or reload your shell configuration:

source ~/.bashrc

Verify the installation:

pixi --version

docs.title: Step 3: Install and Use the Environment
docs.text:
From the root directory of this pipeline, install the Pixi environment:

pixi install

Run commands inside the environment using:

pixi run <command>

For example:

pixi run python --version
pixi run nextflow -version

To enter the environment shell:

pixi shell

If your environment is named illumina2lineage instead of default, use this version:

docs.title: Step 3: Install and Use the Environment
docs.text:
From the root directory of this pipeline, install the Pixi environment:

pixi install -e illumina2lineage

Run commands inside the environment using:

pixi run -e illumina2lineage <command>

For example:

pixi run -e illumina2lineage python --version
pixi run -e illumina2lineage nextflow -version

To enter the environment shell:

pixi shell -e illumina2lineage

docs.title: Set up Java and Nexflow if not already installed
docs.text:
curl -s https://get.sdkman.io | bash

In a new terminal:

sdk install java 17.0.10-tem  
java -version

curl -s https://get.nextflow.io | bash  
chmod +x nextflow 
mkdir -p $HOME/.local/bin/
mv nextflow $HOME/.local/bin/ 
nextflow info

unset JAVA_CMD JAVA_HOME
export JAVA_HOME="$HOME/.sdkman/candidates/java/current"
export JAVA_CMD="$JAVA_HOME/bin/java"

Nextflow requires Bash 3.2 (or later) and Java 17 (or later, up to 24) to be installed. More information on Nextflow installation.

docs.title: Step 4: Run the Pipeline with Nextflow
docs.text: nextflow run main.nf

docs.title: Input Data Requirements
docs.text:
• Illumina paired-end FASTQ files
  • SARS-CoV-2 reference genome (automatically downloaded by the pipeline)

docs.title: Output Overview
docs.text:
• Cleaned FASTQ files and QC reports
  • Sorted, indexed BAM files
  • VCF variant files
  • Consensus sequences (FASTA)
  • Pangolin lineage assignments
  • Phylogenetic tree (Newick format)

For advanced configuration, see the parameters section.

💡 Tip: Use multiqc to summarize all QC results in one place.

You're now ready to use the pipeline!
